current_answer: Choose a skill by the exact frontend task, source revision, agent, and requirements; do not assume adding one improves the result. A web-development preprint found lower average functional pass rates and higher token use when matched skill instructions were injected, while a separate cross-domain benchmark found gains from curated skill access. The studies use different tasks and loading setups, and neither tests this catalogue’s sixteen source-inspected listings or visual quality. For a consequential choice, compare the same project task with a careful no-skill brief and the candidate skill, then inspect the rendered result.

catalogue_card.question: Will a skill improve your web task?
catalogue_card.text: One web-development study found lower average functional scores with injected skill instructions; a cross-domain study found gains from curated skills. Neither tested our listings or visual quality. Compare one real task with and without the skill.

summary: A web-development preprint found mixed skill-project effects and a lower average functional score under prompt-level skill injection.
A separate cross-domain benchmark found gains from curated skill access. Different tasks and loading setups limit direct comparison.
For a consequential frontend task, compare a candidate skill with a careful no-skill brief in the same project and model.
uncertainty: The two benchmark preprints use different tasks and skill-loading setups; neither ranks our sixteen listings or measures their visual quality.
